task: T1: make the loop report its status outward, in scripts/ralph-status.sh. Read two settings from the environment: a base URL from `HARNESS_REPORT_URL` and a bearer token from `HARNESS_REPORT_TOKEN`. When the URL is unset or empty the loop must behave EXACTLY as it does today — write its file, post nothing, and print nothing about it — because `run-loop.sh` has to keep running on a laptop with no infrastructure, and that is the portability bar this whole design is built to clear. When the URL is set, every status the loop already writes is also POSTed as JSON to `{base}/runs/{run_key}/status`, where the run key is the identity the loop already has, `<host>/<agent>-<pid>`; do not mint a second identity, because two names for one run are two names that will disagree. Send the token as an `Authorization: Bearer` header when one is set. Use `curl` when it is available and `python3` otherwise. The POST is fire-and-forget and its own failure must be SILENT and total: an unreachable coordinator, a connection refused, a 500, a timeout — none of them may fail, stall or alter the run, and none may print anything that would be mistaken for a loop error. Bound every call with a short timeout, because a coordinator that accepts a connection and never answers must not hold a build. Add the POST to the existing `hb_write` rather than adding new reporting points; the record and the moments it is written at are already correct and must not change. The token's value must never appear in any output. Do not post attempt records in this task and do not poll for anything; T2 and T3 own those.
